observation_summary: Calling TimeSeries.clone() for an empty series triggers IllegalArgumentException: "Requires start <= end." Stack shows clone() calls createCopy(0, getItemCount() - 1), and createCopy throws when end < start.
reasoning_summary: The failure is caused by a missing boundary/validation check for the empty-series case: clone() unconditionally calls createCopy(0, n-1) which yields end < start when n == 0, and createCopy's guard then throws. The appropriate fix is to add a guard/validation (either in clone() or createCopy()) to handle the empty-case, which makes this a Checking defect.
evidence_used: TimeSeries.createCopy(...): if (end < start) { throw new IllegalArgumentException("Requires start <= end."); } (TimeSeries.java:879-880)
Failing test: testBug1832432 creates an empty TimeSeries and calls clone(), expecting a successful clone (TimeSeriesTests.java:616-626, 629-631)
Bug report description: cloning a TimeSeries which has no items causes IllegalArgumentException and should not require the user to check for empty series.
evidence_gaps: No pre-fix patch or commit provided to show the exact intended code change location (clone() vs createCopy()).
No explicit specification in code comments showing desired behavior when cloning empty series (test and bug report imply expected behavior).

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The incorrect behavior results from an out-of-range parameter (end < start) due to computed indices, not from a wrong constant or mis-initialized variable; fixing requires adding a guard rather than changing an assignment.
The overall copying algorithm is correct for non-empty series; the defect is a missing boundary validation rather than a wrong iteration or computational procedure.
This is an internal method call within the same class (clone -> createCopy) using correct signatures; the problem is parameter bounds, not a boundary/contract mismatch between components.
The failure is deterministic and caused by index/bounds logic, with no concurrency, ordering, or synchronization issues involved.
There is no evidence of inconsistent associations between different data structures or modules—only a local missing check for empty data.
The capability (cloning) exists and behaves correctly for non-empty series; the bug is not a missing class or major design-level capability but a missing guard for a boundary case.
